title: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs
gist: Arm launched the Neoverse CSS N4 compute subsystem — a 3nm, 8-to-128-core design with a CMN S4 chiplet interconnect, PCIe Gen7, and LPDDR6/DDR5/MRDIMM memory support — aimed at next-generation server CPUs and DPUs, while noting how compute subsystems like this let smaller silicon teams (e.g., XSight Labs' 800G DPU) reach market faster and that Arm itself is now fielding its own CPU (the Arm AGI CPU) built on Neoverse V3 cores.

insights.claim: Arm's newly announced Neoverse CSS N4 compute subsystem is built on a 3nm process and supports 8 to 128 cores per die, with Neoverse N4 cores establishing Armv9.3 as the new baseline architecture.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: 128-core-per-die scaling on 3nm sets the core-count ceiling competitors (AMD, Intel, Ampere) will be benchmarked against for next-gen server CPU design wins.
insights.quote: The new Arm Neoverse N4 CSS is built for 3nm process and supports 8 to 128 cores per die.
insights.locator: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs

insights.claim: Neoverse N4 cores are designed to run up to 3.8GHz with a focus on power-efficient compute, and add support for FP8 and MMLA instructions relevant to AI/ML workloads.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: FP8/MMLA support on an efficiency-focused core line signals Arm is pushing AI-inference capability even into its power-efficient (N-series, not just V-series) server core lineup.
insights.quote: These cores are designed to operate at up to 3.8GHz given their focus on power-efficient compute, but also bring support for FP8 and MMLA.
insights.locator: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs

insights.claim: The CSS N4 subsystem uses an Arm Neoverse CMN S4 interconnect fabric supporting up to a 16x16 mesh and fully coherent multi-chiplet connectivity via CHI C2C, tying together CPU cores, memory, I/O, and die-to-die interfaces.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: A coherent multi-chiplet fabric at this scale signals Arm is standardizing chiplet-based, multi-die server CPU construction for its licensees — relevant to tracking chiplet-design convergence across the server CPU industry.
insights.quote: CMN S4 supports up to a 16×16 mesh interconnect and a fully coherent multi-chiplet connectivity using CHI C2C.
insights.locator: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs

insights.claim: The CSS N4 generation adds support for LPDDR6 memory alongside DDR5 and MRDIMMs at 8000-12000 MT/s speeds, plus up to 128 lanes of PCIe Gen7.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Concrete memory/IO spec set to benchmark against competing server platforms once silicon based on CSS N4 ships.
insights.quote: On the memory side, this new generation also brings support for both LPDDR6 memory as well as DDR5 and MRDIMMs at 8000-12000MT/s speeds.
insights.locator: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs

insights.claim: Because CSS N4 includes PCIe Gen7 support, actual CPUs built on this subsystem are likely at least one product generation away from shipping, since PCIe Gen7 is ahead of what current-generation server CPUs implement.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Sets investor expectations that CSS N4-based server CPUs and DPUs are a multi-year-out story, not a near-term product catalyst.
insights.quote: For I/O, there are up to 128 lanes of PCIe Gen7 which also tells us that this is designed for CPUs coming out in at least one generation from now.
insights.locator: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs

themes.theme: CSS lowers the barrier for custom-silicon entrants

insights.claim: XSight Labs' E1 64-core Arm 800G DPU is a real, shipping example of an Arm Neoverse CSS N2 implementation, built with 64 Arm Neoverse N2 cores.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: A concrete production design win validates Arm's CSS licensing model for DPU/network-silicon startups, ahead of the newer CSS N4 generation.
insights.quote: This is an Arm Neoverse CSS N2 design with 64 Arm Neoverse N2 cores.
insights.locator: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs

insights.claim: For a silicon startup like XSight Labs, licensing Arm's Neoverse CSS compute subsystem rather than designing custom cores from scratch lets a small engineering team reach market faster, since Arm handles much of the base design work.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: CSS licensing lowers the capital and engineering barrier to entry for custom DPU/network-silicon, which could accelerate fragmentation and new-entrant competition in that market segment.
insights.quote: For a startup like XSight Labs, using a Neoverse CSS design makes a lot of sense, since Arm does much of the base design work, helping a smaller team get to market faster.
insights.locator: Arm Neoverse CSS N4 Launched for Next-Gen CPUs and DPUs

insights.claim: Although Arm's Neoverse V-series line tends to get more industry attention, the N-series of cores has become especially popular in product lines like DPUs and network appliances.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Real design-win volume for Arm may be concentrating in the less-publicized N-series/DPU segment rather than the headline V-series server-CPU segment — worth weighing when assessing where Arm's server-silicon revenue actually comes from.
insights.quote: While it is often the Neoverse V-series line making headlines, the N-series of cores has become very popular in product lines like DPUs and network appliances.

themes.theme: Arm's move into building its own CPU

insights.claim: Arm is now building its own CPU, the Arm AGI CPU, using Neoverse V3 cores — moving beyond its traditional role of licensing IP to fielding its own silicon.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Arm building its own CPU is a strategic shift that could put it in more direct competition with its own CSS/Neoverse licensees (e.g., hyperscaler custom-silicon teams) — a potential channel-conflict risk worth monitoring for Arm's licensing business model.
insights.quote: Arm is also making its own CPUs now, with the Arm AGI CPU that is using Neoverse V3 cores.
